chunks: From him, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Aban, from Mansur, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who bought a sale in which there is no measuring (by volume) nor weighing. Is it permissible for him to sell it via murabahah (profit-sharing/margin sale) before he takes possession of it and takes his profit? He said: 'There is no harm in that, provided there is no measuring nor weighing. If he takes possession, then he is free of liability for himself.'
ai.seo_question: Can I sell goods before taking possession if they are not measured or weighed?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between generic goods (not defined by weight or measure) and specific items, permitting pre-possession sale (murabahah) for the former to facilitate trade while noting that actual possession (qabd) absolves the seller of residual risk. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on 'qabd' (possession) as the critical factor determining liability in sales contracts, ensuring that the seller is not held responsible for loss before the goods are effectively under their control.
